secondary_finding_receipt_self_hash.claim: artifacts[].sha256 is defined as 'the artifact bytes as they exist on disk', which is unsatisfiable for a receipt that describes itself. Measured: 37 of 37 sibling ADV receipts record a primary hash that does not match their own bytes (byte COUNTS agree, so this is the self-reference paradox, not truncation). SNAPSHOT SCOPE: peer agents were writing sibling receipts while this unit ran, so the denominator moved during the session (35 -> 37); the finding is the ZERO numerator, which does not depend on it.
secondary_finding_receipt_self_hash.why_it_matters: predicate condition 3 ('the recorded sha256 equals the hash of the bytes on disk') can never pass for a primary self-reference, so any receipt claiming SUCCESS on it is claiming a check that cannot have run.
